faq.a: One of the two named experts. Both work under a codename while employed elsewhere; after payment you receive their real name, photo and LinkedIn before the call is scheduled.

faq.q: Why not just use an AI screening tool?
faq.a: Because candidates use AI too. Automated tools grade the answer, not the person giving it. A live conversation with follow-up questions is currently the only reliable way to tell lived experience from a well-written script.

faq.q: What if we hire the candidate?
faq.a: Nothing changes. We charge per screen, not per hire. We are not a recruiting agency and take no placement fee.
Not at the order. We confirm an expert has a slot first, then send a payment link. If we cannot schedule inside the window, you are not charged at all.

faq.q: What happens to the candidate's data?
faq.a: The CV is used for the screen and deleted on request. The assessment goes to you alone. We take a transcript of the call, never a recording; it is deleted 30 days after delivery. We never publish or sell candidate data.
A small team building infrastructure for verified human reputation. Verified.Ninja is the first commercial service built on it — there is more on the about page.

about.title: Part of something larger
about.lede: Verified.Ninja is the first commercial service built on one idea: a person whose experience has actually been checked is worth more than a person who claims it. This page exists so you know who is behind the screen you are buying. It changes nothing about the service itself.

layers.d: Technical screening by senior engineers. What you are looking at. It pays for everything below.
Facts and analysis written by verified experts and reviewed by other verified people. Reputation earned through work, not bought.
Short observations from real people only. Protection against fakes, sold as a service.

found: Underneath all three sits an open project called WorldConstitution: a charter, a reputation that belongs to the person rather than to a platform, and a protocol for confirming that someone is a real, single human being.

It is a social project, not a company, and it makes no money. The commercial services exist to prove the idea works in practice — companies pay for a verified human, which is the only argument that counts.
Wiki and Feed are plans, not promises. There is no token, no token sale is planned, and we make no promises of income to anyone.
about.honestT: Why this is on a separate page
about.honest: Because it is not your problem. When you buy a screen, what matters is who runs the call, what the report says and when it arrives. Nothing about the parent project appears on an expert's profile or inside your report — that is a rule we hold ourselves to, not a preference.
